note: 30-45 correct / 25-30 borderline / <25 incorrect are PROJECT_SPEC. The 45-55 upper borderline band is an ENGINEERING_DEFAULT: the specification lists no 'too deep' Aramandi error, deeper bends are recognised as Muzhumandi instead.
Band widths are PROJECT_SPEC. The target separation itself (0.6 shoulder widths) is an ENGINEERING_DEFAULT.
Pelvic symmetry band mirrors the foot-line band; not fixed by spec.
Deviation from a 45deg turnout target. Wider than the 8/15 orientation band because monocular turnout estimation from a heel-to-toe vector is noisy.
PROJECT_SPEC bands, applied to the gap between the feet. The feet-together baseline (0.3 shoulder widths of ankle-to-ankle distance) is DATA_CALIBRATED.
Foot orientation deviation from the 0deg (parallel, forward) target.

The specification deliberately fixes no numeric band here. This is a landmark-based lateral weight-shift PROXY (offset of the shoulder/pelvis midline from the ankle midline); it does not measure ground reaction force.
Secondary loading proxy used together with weight_shift_proxy.
Knee/foot orientation deviation from the 45deg turnout target; detects the 'feet and knees facing forward' error.

The specification says to 'check whether the required heel configuration is maintained' without a number. Heel lift is measured as the toe-to-heel vertical offset normalised by shoulder width; a heel pressed on the floor gives ~0.
Supports the 'feet far apart and heel pressing on floor' error.
Legs must actually cross; a large gap means they never met.
Signed ankle gap; strongly negative values indicate OVERCROSSED shins. Interpreted from the labelled samples, not from literature.
Lower bound on the signed ankle gap: below it the shins overcross.
Swastikapadam is held in Aramandi depth, so the Aramandi PROJECT_SPEC flexion range is reused to detect 'insufficient Aramandi'.
Reported for the record. No universal published crossing-angle threshold exists, so this band is NOT used to fail a posture on its own.
Pataka keeps the fingers together; spread detects 'fingers too far apart'.
Alapadma is a fully splayed lotus hand: fingers must be spread.
Mushti is a closed fist, so the long fingers must be strongly flexed.
Pinky tip-to-palm distance divided by the mean of the other three fingers; detects 'pinky dropped / fingers loose'.
Katakamukha joins the thumb to the index and middle fingertips.
The ring and little fingers stay extended in Katakamukha, so the PROJECT_SPEC finger-straightness range applies to them; a drop below it is the 'fingers bent' error.
